speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I need to assess the newborn presenting with respiratory distress. How many hours old is the infant, and was the pregnancy full-term?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Doctor
text: Was there any delay in the clearance of fetal lung fluid, and did the infant exhibit grunting or nasal flaring immediately after birth? I also need to know if the mother received antenatal corticosteroids during pregnancy.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Tachypnea, Subcostal and intercostal retractions, Nasal flaring, Cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray
REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest_X-Ray: Ground-glass appearance, air bronchograms, suggesting Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS). Arterial_Blood_Gas: pH 7.30 (slightly acidic), PaCO2 50 mm Hg (elevated), PaO2 60 mm Hg (reduced), HCO3- 24 mEq/L, Base_Excess -5.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of prematurity, maternal diabetes, and classic RDS findings on X-ray confirms the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome
